annotations.description: The choice between Sowing Mycospawn and Shifting Woodland from Malevolent Rumble is debatable. Sowing Mycospawn is a strong card that searches for a land when cast and can exile a land if kicked, but Coach already has two Talismans in hand and could use more colored mana sources. Shifting Woodland is a land that provides green mana and has a powerful delirium ability (becoming a copy of a permanent in graveyard). However, Coach already has 5 card types in graveyard (land, instant, sorcery, creature from Stomping Ground/Kozilek's Return/Malevolent Rumble/Verdant Catacombs) - actually checking: Land (Verdant Catacombs, Stomping Ground), Instant (Kozilek's Return x2), Sorcery (Malevolent Rumble) = 3 types, not 4 yet. With Talisman of Impulse already available to pick, taking Sowing Mycospawn is reasonable as it's a powerful Eldrazi creature that ramps and disrupts. Sowing Mycospawn also triggers Kozilek's Return from graveyard (MV 5, not 7+, so no). Actually Sowing Mycospawn has MV 4, so no Kozilek's Return trigger. The Mycospawn does search for a land when cast, which is good ramp. However, Shifting Woodland could have been valuable as a free land drop that enables delirium plays later. Coach already has enough mana sources in hand (2 Talismans) but needs lands. Taking Shifting Woodland as a land that enters untapped (since Coach controls a Forest) might have been comparable or better since Coach can play it immediately for mana while deploying a Talisman too. But Sowing Mycospawn's land search is also strong. This is close enough to be debatable.

However, Sowing Mycospawn's land search when cast is also powerful ramp, making this genuinely debatable.

annotations.description: Playing Wooded Foothills (an untapped fetch) on turn 3 instead of Thundering Falls (which always enters tapped) is a sequencing error. Thundering Falls should be played now while there's no immediate mana need, preserving the fetch for a turn where untapped mana matters. Additionally, Thundering Falls provides the U source needed for Omnath turn 4, while Wooded Foothills cannot fetch blue. The surveil from Thundering Falls also helps build the graveyard for Phlage escape.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Wooded Foothills as the turn 3 land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Thundering Falls (enters tapped, provides U for Omnath next turn, surveil helps graveyard), saving fetch lands for turns where untapped mana is needed

annotations.description: GLM47 Coach cast Sowing Mycospawn without kicker when they could have kicked it by playing Ugin's Labyrinth first. Playing the land first would give: Forest (G) + Eldrazi Temple (CC for Eldrazi) + Talisman (C) + new Ugin's Labyrinth (C) + Eldrazi Spawn sacrifice (C) = exactly {4}{G}{C}, enough for Sowing Mycospawn ({3}{G}) with kicker ({1}{C}). Kicking it would exile one of the opponent's lands when they only have 3 lands, a devastating tempo play against an opponent at 12 life trying to escape Phlage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sowing Mycospawn without playing Ugin's Labyrinth first, missing the opportunity to kick it.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ugin's Labyrinth first, then cast Sowing Mycospawn with kicker using Forest + Eldrazi Temple + Talisman + Ugin's Labyrinth + Eldrazi Spawn sacrifice, exiling one of the opponent's key lands (like Breeding Pool or Temple Garden).

annotations.description: GLM47 Coach passed their turn without playing a land or casting any spells, despite having Ghost Quarter/Ugin's Labyrinth available as land drops and Talisman of Impulse castable with available mana. They need to ramp toward casting Sowing Mycospawn (and eventually recovering Ugin), so missing both a land drop and a mana rock deployment is a meaningful setback.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without playing a land or casting anything.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ghost Quarter (preserving it for utility against opponent's lands), then cast Talisman of Impulse using Forest + Eldrazi Temple for {2}. This adds two mana sources and puts them much closer to casting kicked Sowing Mycospawn next turn.

annotations.description: GLM47 Coach has a land drop available (Forest, Ghost Quarter, or Ugin's Labyrinth) and chose to pass without playing one. They have Sowing Mycospawn in hand which costs {3}{G} with kicker {1}{C}, and accelerating mana is important for casting it next turn (potentially kicked). Playing Forest would provide an additional green source, and there's no reason to hold it since it enters untapped. Missing a land drop when you have lands in hand and expensive spells to cast is a clear mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without playing a land, despite having Forest, Ghost Quarter, and Ugin's Labyrinth in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest (or possibly Ghost Quarter for utility) to develop mana and enable casting Sowing Mycospawn next turn, potentially with kicker using Eldrazi Temple and spawn token.

annotations.description: Cracking Arid Mesa before casting Wrenn and Six means losing a potential landfall trigger for Omnath next turn. Wrenn's +1 could recur a fetchland from graveyard, giving an extra land drop for Omnath landfall. Saving fetches for Omnath turns is important for maximizing the landfall chain (4 life, then RGWU mana, then 4 damage).
annotations.actionTaken: Cracked Arid Mesa first before casting any spells
annotations.betterLine: Cast Wrenn and Six first (RG from Temple Garden + Sacred Foundry), +1 to return a fetchland from graveyard to hand, then decide whether to crack Arid Mesa now or save it for Omnath landfall triggers next turn.

annotations.description: Eldrazi Temple's second ability produces {C}{C} that can only be spent on colorless Eldrazi spells or abilities. Kozilek's Return is a colorless Instant (via Devoid) but does not have the Eldrazi subtype, so the restricted mana cannot be used to cast it. Choosing the restricted mana mode wastes potential value from the Temple.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Eldrazi Temple's second ability ({C}{C} restricted to colorless Eldrazi spells) to help pay for Kozilek's Return
annotations.betterLine: Choose Eldrazi Temple's first ability ({C} unrestricted) since Kozilek's Return is not an Eldrazi spell and cannot use the restricted mana

annotations.description: GLM47 Coach chose to exile Teferi, Time Raveler instead of Wrenn and Six with Ugin's cast trigger. Teferi is at 1 loyalty and can only bounce/draw once more before dying, while Wrenn and Six is at 4 loyalty and provides recurring land recursion (fueling Phlage escapes and fixing) and threatens an ultimate. Wrenn and Six is the more impactful long-term threat. However, Teferi's static ability prevents Coach from casting spells at instant speed (each opponent can cast spells only any time they could cast a sorcery), which matters less now that Ugin is resolving. Teferi also could bounce Ugin with its -3, which would be devastating. That said, Teferi at 1 loyalty is very fragile and Gramps' lands are all tapped, so the bounce threat isn't immediate. Wrenn at 4 loyalty is much harder to remove and provides more sustained value.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Teferi, Time Raveler (1 loyalty) with Ugin's cast trigger
annotations.betterLine: Exile Wrenn and Six (4 loyalty), which is a more durable and impactful threat. Teferi at 1 loyalty could be dealt with by Ugin's ongoing triggered ability on the next colorless spell, or would die to any incidental damage.

annotations.description: Exiled fetch lands (Arid Mesa, 2x Flooded Strand) from graveyard for Phlage's escape cost while Wrenn and Six is on the battlefield at 4 loyalty, capable of recurring those fetch lands every turn for repeated landfall triggers and mana fixing.
annotations.actionTaken: Exiled Arid Mesa and both Flooded Strands (valuable Wrenn and Six recursion targets) as part of Phlage's escape cost.
annotations.betterLine: Exile cards with no graveyard utility instead, such as Solitude, Malevolent Rumble, Prismatic Ending, Forest, and Delighted Halfling, preserving fetch lands for Wrenn and Six's +1 ability to generate recurring value.

annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without playing Ghost Quarter or activating Ugin's Labyrinth.
annotations.betterLine: Play Ghost Quarter as the land for the turn to advance toward casting Emrakul. Could also activate the untapped Ugin's Labyrinth to return Ugin, Eye of the Storms to hand for future use.
